Subject: Re: Pilot benchmarks & acceptance — initial draft

Elaine — thanks for the draft. Quick response from our side with a proposed workload charter and acceptance criteria that we can bake into the MAP. If this looks good we'll add it to the shared MAP and start scheduling test windows.

Proposed workload slices (examples):
1) Short chat (mean prompt tokens 20, response 30): 60% of requests. Target p95 generation latency: <=200ms; TTFT (first stream) <=500ms warm, <=1200ms cold.
2) Long form (mean prompt tokens 250, response 400): 30% of requests. Target p95 generation latency: <=1.5s; TTFT <=1.2s warm, <=2.5s cold.
3) Embeddings/Vectorization (batch workloads): 10% of requests. Throughput target: 6k tokens/sec (aggregate) under sustained load.

Concurrency & throughput SLOs:
- Sustained concurrency baseline: 200 concurrent requests with target average latency within SLOs.
- Burst capacity: 500 concurrent connections for up to 2 minutes during peak with graceful degradation and documented fallback model.

Quality / success criteria:
- Generation quality regressions: must be <=1% measurable delta on Atlas evaluation set (we'll use your 1000-sample prompt set).
- Error rate (5xx) must be <0.5% during any 10-minute window.
- TTFT p95 thresholds above.

Acceptance gates:
A) Pilot run complete (engineer verification) — sign-off by Aditya.
B) MAP performance report reviewed — sign-off by Atlas engineering (Elaine) + Redwood Solutions (Grace).
C) Business decision (procurement/legal) — contract exercise or rollback.

Attachments: pilot-workload-def.md (contains test harness details, sequence length distributions, batching profiles).

Next steps: Aditya, can you review the target numbers and list any baseline test infra we should stand up (load generator, KV warm-up steps, observability hooks)? Also adding a 2-week execution buffer in the MAP once DocuSign is complete.

Thanks,
Steph

Thanks Stephanie — quick technical notes and a proposed execution plan. I quoted your message below for context.

Quoted: 
> Proposed workload slices (examples):
> 1) Short chat ... p95 generation latency: <=200ms; TTFT <=500ms warm ...

Notes / clarifications:
- Warm vs cold: our TTFT delta is primarily driven by KV cache warm-up on LLMs with long context. For short chat (20/30 tokens) warm/cold difference should be <300ms after a short warm-up load. For long-form, plan to run a 10-minute warm-up per model variant before recording steady-state metrics.
- Sequence length distribution: we'll use three buckets (0-64, 65-512, 513-2048) and weight them 60/30/10 respectively unless Atlas wants a custom distribution. Please confirm.
- Batching and quantization: to hit 6k tokens/s we'll rely on continuous batching and 16-bit kernels on NVR-optimized nodes; throughput numbers are achievable but will show higher TTFT for small, latency-sensitive requests unless we prioritize low-latency routing.
- Concurrency ramp: 0 -> 200 over 10 minutes, hold 20 minutes, then 200 -> 500 for 2 minutes (burst), then cool down. We'll capture p50/p95/p99 latencies, TTFT streams, 5xx counts, and token/sec.

Test infra we need from Atlas:
- A representative 1k prompt sample (already mentioned) in JSON-lines format.
- Typical QPS curve and business hours window (timezone).
- Any extremely long prompts (>2k tokens) flagged as special case.

Deliverables:
- Raw run logs + aggregated metrics (CSV)
- MAP performance report (PDF) with SLO pass/fail matrix and recommendations
- Suggested fallback configurations for production rollout (routing by latency/cost)

I'll schedule a stub test cluster and share access for verification. Ping me for any extra telemetry fields you want tracked.

- Aditya
